sense: real, complete, as it should be

terms.gloss: proper, complete, regular, of the right size
evidence: Caes. B.C. 1.23: iter jūstum, a regular day’s march (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 9.43: exercitus, an army at full strength (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is just, righteous. Of things it means proper and complete: a full army, a regular battle, a wall of the proper height (Caes. B.G. 7.23) (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Suet. Dom. 7: rēctārum cēnārum cōnsuētūdō (Lewis & Short, s.v. regō)
terms.comment: Cēna rēcta is a proper, formal dinner (Lewis & Short). Otherwise rēctus is straight, or right and correct (see correct).

phrases.english: to fight a proper, regular battle

phrases.latin: Hodiē rēctam cēnam nōn parāvī; pānis et cāseus satis erunt.
phrases.english: I haven’t made a proper dinner today; bread and cheese will have to do.

sources: Lewis & Short: justus · Lewis & Short: rego
